title: PairLift: Interaction-Separating Corrections for Closed-Loop VLA Control
hook: Two correctors can have identical center gradients and every single-channel FastWAM response yet prefer opposite bimanual edits. PairLift predicts higher RoboTwin task success only when the mixed response is allowed to choose the joint correction itself.
hook_shape_rationale: Shape (a), surprising empirical reveal: the named metric is RoboTwin task success, and the predicted regime split is between axis-equivalent response surfaces whose interaction-aware joint edits differ. Shape (c) was viable because PairLift freezes the VLA and world model, but rejected because its joint probes use more inference than an ordinary center-gradient corrector.

gap_closure.sub_pattern: C10 (Characterize a Limit, Then Surpass It)
gap_closure.how_closed: Corpus support is thin for closed-loop VLA correction and C10's closest exemplars are relational expressivity limits; PairLift instantiates its abstract move by proving an axis-response indistinguishability class, then surpassing it with mixed finite differences that enter a support-two quadratic correction, while reframe_as_solvable_object turns that augmentation into an exact analytic box-QP update.

core_mechanism: At a RoboTwin control state o_t, a frozen OpenPI π0.5 checkpoint emits its native action chunk a^0, and its published action schema partitions coordinates into left and right channel-trajectories G_L and G_R; for each group g, h_g is the proprioceptive hold trajectory and a(δ)_g=h_g+(1+δ_g)(a^0_g-h_g), clipped to the native action box. A frozen FastWAM rollout followed by a logistic outcome head q_φ, trained and held-out calibrated on RoboTwin's existing simulator task-success predicate, supplies Q(δ)=E_ξ[q_φ(F_ψ(o_t,a(δ),ξ))], where ξ is a common stochastic rollout seed and the expectation is estimated with K_ξ=4 seeds by default, chosen as the smallest held-out seed count whose action-variant ranking stabilizes. The axis probe radius ε defaults to 0.10 in the dimensionless scaling coordinate and is selected from a held-out sweep by minimizing FastWAM-versus-executed RoboTwin rank disagreement; q_0=Q(0), m_g=[Q(εe_g)-Q(-εe_g)]/(2ε), and d_g=[Q(εe_g)-2q_0+Q(-εe_g)]/ε^2. The incumbent interaction-free class A_axis is any corrector whose decision is measurable only from q_0 and the restrictions {Q(te_g)}_g: for any cross-effector pair (g,h), adding c·δ_gδ_h leaves every such restriction and the center gradient unchanged while changing the best joint edit, giving an explicit axis-equivalence separation witness rather than an informal claim that gradients are weak. PairLift breaks that equivalence with I_gh=[Q(εe_g+εe_h)-Q(εe_g-εe_h)-Q(-εe_g+εe_h)+Q(-εe_g-εe_h)]/(4ε^2) for every (g,h) in G_L×G_R. It then makes I load-bearing by maximizing S_gh(x,y)=q_0+m_gx+m_hy+(d_gx^2+d_hy^2)/2+I_ghxy over (x,y) in [-r,r]^2 for each cross-effector pair, where r defaults to 0.20 and is selected on held-out RoboTwin states for the best executed-success-versus-action-deviation trade-off; the global update is the best pair solution or the zero update. Each two-dimensional box quadratic is solved exactly by evaluating its feasible interior stationary point, edge stationary points, and corners, so all pairs cost O(|G_L||G_R|) arithmetic after the probes and no nonconvex high-dimensional solver is assumed. Because two response surfaces can share m and all axis restrictions but differ in I, they induce different PairLift actions while every same-budget A_axis baseline—given repeated axis probes to match FastWAM calls—must emit the same action on both. A final common-seed FastWAM rollout compares a(δ*) with a^0 and executes the correction only when its predicted success is higher; restored-state RoboTwin E0 executions separately test whether this interaction-caused action difference improves actual task success.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 — PREMISES ledger:
P1. In the calibrated neighborhood, FastWAM plus q_φ preserves the ordering of nearby action variants often enough to select a correction; common-state and common-seed evaluation makes this plausible, but it is untested — falsification target through I.
P2. A support-two quadratic response captures the load-bearing local cross-effector interaction even when the full dynamics is higher-order; this is untested — falsification target, and claims are restricted to the ε and r neighborhood.
P3. OpenPI's native left/right action schema provides stable channel groups without learned role labels, so group identity does not assume acting/stabilizing roles.
OBSERVATION-MODEL premise. States are sampled from frozen π0.5 RoboTwin rollouts, action variants are generated independently of their outcomes, and ξ is coupled across variants; this targets the frozen-policy occupancy rather than all possible robot states, while FastWAM and q_φ errors may bias Q and are therefore audited against restored-state simulator execution.
ESTIMAND. For fixed (o_t,a^0), m, d, and I are the central first, diagonal-second, and cross-second finite differences of predicted RoboTwin success Q over proposal-relative channel scalings, averaged over the declared FastWAM seed process; E0 estimates the paired executed-success effect of the action selected from those quantities, not a global causal effect.
BLOCK 2 — NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT. The runnable naive mechanism spends its budget on single-channel ±ε FastWAM probes, estimates a center gradient, and selects up to two channel scalings by an additive response model. Branch (i): it silently assumes that the axis restrictions determine the best joint correction, which is false because c·δ_gδ_h vanishes on every axis yet reverses joint rankings; PairLift confronts this by querying the four joint signs and retaining I_ghxy inside the action objective rather than reducing I to a center gradient. Finite differences and box quadratics are standard tools, but the domain-specific structure is a frozen temporally chunked VLA proposal observed through a stochastic WAM proxy under native action bounds, with the mixed term required to alter the executed chunk and its sign audited by restored-state simulator outcomes; the contribution is this action-native separation-and-correction operator, not generic response-surface fitting.
BLOCK 3 — Design rationale. An anchor-only chain was chosen because the separation witness and the correction share the same response object; adding a role-reversal or field-wide assumption-audit leg would require separate machinery and would not strengthen the anchor's falsifier. Full factorial ANOVA, COMA credit, Shapley allocation, and preset coordination graphs were rejected because they either stop at attribution or regress to occupied lineage nodes instead of defining an action-changing separation. Cross-run mechanisms are also distinct: PairLift has no CBSM feasibility-flip boundary score, GISS geometry–action crossover, ExitReplay censoring replay, or ScaffoldFracture fixed-scaffold regret; its sole new object is native-action mixed curvature that remains inside the correction objective.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Freeze the existing OpenPI π0.5 and FastWAM checkpoints; collect frozen-policy RoboTwin states, FastWAM rollout features, and the simulator's existing task-success labels, then fit and held-out calibrate q_φ. Inputs: RGB, proprioception, language goal, action chunks, simulator labels; output: frozen q_φ with calibration provenance.
2. Parse the OpenPI action schema into G_L and G_R, construct the hold chunk h from current proprioception, and implement the proposal-relative scaling map a(δ) with native box clipping. Inputs: checkpoint schema, a^0, proprioception; outputs: typed channel groups and a callable action map.
3. On disjoint RoboTwin calibration states, select ε, r, and K_ξ by the rules stated in core_mechanism and record every candidate value, rank disagreement, executed outcome, latency, and memory use. Inputs: frozen checkpoints and calibration states; outputs: bound parameters and audit records.
4. For each E0 state, evaluate q_0 and all ±ε axis probes with coupled FastWAM seeds, then compute m and d; cache every rollout so the same-budget axis baseline receives exactly the same total FastWAM-call allowance through additional axis-seed replications. Inputs: o_t, a^0, a(·), F_ψ, q_φ; outputs: q_0, m, d, and matched-budget baseline records.
5. Evaluate the four signed joint probes for every pair in G_L×G_R and compute I with the stated mixed finite difference; never infer I from m or collapse it into a center gradient. Inputs: cached axis scores plus joint FastWAM scores; output: the cross-effector interaction matrix I with seed-wise uncertainty.
6. Materialize the axis-equivalence witness by pairing the fitted response with its I=0 counterpart: verify that q_0, every axis score, m, and d match while at least one pairwise quadratic ranking changes; if none changes, emit no_separation_at_state and retain a^0. Inputs: m, d, I, probe table; output: a per-state checkable separation certificate.
7. For every cross-effector pair, enumerate the analytic interior, edge, and corner candidates of S_gh over [-r,r]^2, select the global support-two maximizer δ*, and serialize which I_gh term changed the winning action relative to I=0. Inputs: q_0, m, d, I, r; outputs: δ*, predicted gain, winning pair, and an interaction-dependence trace.
8. Re-evaluate a(δ*) and a^0 with the same FastWAM seeds and pass the corrected chunk to execution only if q_φ assigns it higher predicted success; otherwise retain a^0. Inputs: candidate and baseline chunks; output: the executed chunk and accept/retain record.
9. In restored-state RoboTwin E0, execute a^0, the same-budget axis-only corrector, PairLift, and the partner-permuted-I negative control; log task success, correction latency, selected channel pair, predicted gain, and executed gain. Inputs: saved simulator states and four arms; outputs: paired downstream outcomes and an I-to-action-to-success audit.
falsification_prediction: On existing RoboTwin bimanual contact tasks, restore identical simulator states and seeds for one frozen OpenPI π0.5 checkpoint and one frozen FastWAM checkpoint, then compare the frozen proposal, a same-FastWAM-call axis-only center-gradient corrector, and PairLift. If the mechanism works, RoboTwin task success increases for PairLift specifically on states carrying an axis-equivalence separation certificate, while correction latency is reported rather than thresholded. The single load-bearing variable is the cross-effector mixed-response matrix I; as a negative control, permute its right-channel partner labels before solving while keeping q_0, m, d, FastWAM calls, seeds, r, and the analytic solver unchanged. This preserves marginal information and compute but breaks which joint edit the mixed response supports, and the prediction is that downstream RoboTwin task success returns toward the same-budget axis-only/frozen-policy baseline.
compute_budget: 18 A100-40GB GPU-days (approximately 9 80GB-class GPU-days) for outcome-head fitting, coupled FastWAM probes, held-out parameter selection, and restored-state RoboTwin E0; $0 paid API for the full campaign. This is comfortable within the stated four-A100 rollback-first envelope, with expansion beyond E0 gated on the separation certificate and executed-success check.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: Abstract-only evidence: CoCo enforces and measures whole-action counterfactual responsiveness, whereas PairLift defines an axis-response equivalence class that whole-action responsiveness cannot separate and constructs a mixed-curvature correction whose selected action changes with I.

Abstract-only evidence: ω-EVA refines a whole proposal from its latent predicted future, whereas PairLift exhibits two proposals with identical axis-visible evidence but different joint optima and inserts the separating mixed response directly into the action update.

Abstract-only evidence: the optimizer interaction calculus identifies Boolean effects for declared optimizer response classes, whereas PairLift defines the native continuous action-chunk equivalence class, an O(|G_L||G_R|) support-two surpass operator, and an executed RoboTwin action consequence.

Abstract-only evidence: the policy-aware factorial design uses low-rank tensor completion and marginal elimination to choose intervention bundles, whereas PairLift uses exact local mixed contrasts to choose a bounded action correction and makes their partner identity falsifiable at execution.

Abstract-only evidence: ManiGaussian++ fixes acting and stabilizing roles in a leader–follower world model, whereas PairLift derives state-local cross-effector channel pairs without permanent roles and can select different joint supports at different states.

what_step_was_missed: It would have needed to define indistinguishability on a frozen VLA's native axis-restricted action responses, re-inject the resulting cross-effector mixed finite difference into a support-two box-constrained action update, and verify that the changed action improves restored-state robot task success.
